title: A button grows to fit the words in it
goal: Giving a button a longer label leaves the button the same width, so the words spill out of it or sit cramped. A container should be able to size itself to what is inside, with padding around it, so a longer label makes the button wider and everything stays laid out.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-04 alongside the lost text bug: the button does not grow with content like you would expect. Today a container has placement (LayerPlacement.swift, shipped 2026-09-03: Left, Center, Right, Stretch and the vertical pair, with Scale as the unset default) but no notion of sizing to contents. This is the hug half of the layout story the design study calls auto layout (docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-build-screen.html: direction, gap, padding, hug and fill); full auto layout with stacking and gaps stays deferred per docs/design/ui-building.md, but hug plus padding is the piece that makes a component usable and should land alone. Order it after the knobs task so a wording change is a real edit before it has to drive a resize. Watch the interaction with placement: a hugging container has no spare room, so Stretch on a child inside one needs a defined meaning; write it into the spec.
acceptance: A group or frame can be set to size itself to its contents, on either axis independently, with padding on all four sides
Changing the wording of a starter button makes the button wider and keeps its padding, with no manual resizing
A container set to a fixed size behaves exactly as it does today, and existing documents are unchanged
The layout settles in one pass: nothing jitters or requires a second edit to look right
Core logic covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation
Audit written under queue/audits/ showing a starter button with a short and a long label, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Reproduced first, in a test: drop a starter Button (128x36), re-word its Label to 'Save all the changes now' and reflow. The label re-measures to 189 wide and lands at x=-29; the Background pill stays 128 wide at x=0. So the words really do spill out both sides. The pieces that were missing are (1) nothing tells a plain group to close around its contents, and (2) nothing tells a background to follow a box that grew.

Adversarial pass on the idea before building. (1) The mock's per-child Hug/Fill/Fixed row stays cut: the Horizontal and Vertical placement rows already say it, and a second control that says the same thing is how two controls start disagreeing. (2) Hug for a SCREEN is deliberately not built: a screen's box is the box you drew, and something hanging off its edge must never resize it, which is the whole point of a screen. Cards and buttons are groups, so the feature lands where it is actually wanted. (3) The one real question the task named, answered: a container that hugs has no spare room, so a piece told to Stretch inside one cannot be measured (it would be sizing itself to itself) and cannot be placed (there is nothing to place it against). So a stretched piece is not measured on the axis it stretches, and a piece that stretches BOTH ways is the surface behind everything, painted to the box's edges rather than taking a turn in the arrangement. That is exactly what a button's background is. (4) Shortest version that delivers it: Free groups gain the Hug/Fixed and Padding rows a Stack already has, the surface rule lands once for every kind, and the starter Button is rebuilt on it. The card, nav bar and text field need real layout decisions of their own and get a follow-up task rather than being redrawn blind.

Built it. GroupLayout.kind is optional now: nil is Free, a group that arranges nothing and closes around what is in it, and Free gains the Hug/Fixed rows and the Padding field that used to belong to a stack alone. The spec the task asked for is written into docs/design/ui-building.md and into the code: a stretched piece is not measured on the axis it stretches, and a piece that stretches both ways is the surface behind everything, painted to the container's own edges rather than to the room inside them. The starter Button (16 either side, 36 tall) and Badge are built on it. Two things found on the way and fixed: a container has to measure the WORDS, not the four points of slack a measured text box carries on its far edges, or a centred label sits two points off; and StarterComponents had a second text estimate that disagreed with TextMeasurement by one point, which made a starter's label read as a paragraph somebody had narrowed, so a longer word wrapped down the page instead of widening the button. 3050 tests green.

Adversarial pass on the built thing, in the probe app (Scripts/playtest/button-hug-walk.json, Screen Recording granted so the audit carries real captures). Found a real break: typing a padding bigger than the height the group was given squashed the pill to nothing, and a shape squashed to no height can never be given one back, so the button and its copy vanished. Fixed twice over: the surface is placed once from the box rather than being squeezed into the room inside the edges first, and nothing that has a size is ever handed a box with none. Covered by a test. Two papercuts I could not fix inside this task, both filed: double clicking a copy's words puts the caret at the end so typing appends (the walk's button reads 'ButtonSave all the changes'), and a copy still offers a Layout section whose numbers are thrown away at the next sync. Also filed: the card, nav bar and text field still hold the size they were drawn at.

Every group can be told to be the size of what is inside it, with room on all four sides, and a piece set to Stretch both ways is the surface behind the rest rather than something that sets the size. The starter Button and Badge are built on it, so a longer label makes a wider button with nothing to drag. Core in GroupFlow/GroupLayout/Layer (PhotonzCore), rows in ArrangementInspector. TDD in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/GroupHugTests.swift; 3050 tests green; walked in the probe app with Scripts/playtest/button-hug-walk.json, which found and fixed a break where room bigger than a fixed height squashed the fill away. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-04-ui-hug.json with two real captures. Three follow-ups filed.
